claims.text: Water quenching immediately after annealing arrests diffusion-driven coarsening and phase transformation in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Water quenching retains a metastable phase mixture with a fine-scale distribution of FCC/BCC interphase boundaries.
A fine metastable interphase structure can optimally balance high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Phase mixing is active near an annealing temperature of 1000°C.
Slow furnace cooling permits equilibrium phase formation.
Metastable phase boundaries and nanoscale precipitates arise from non-equilibrium interruption of phase transformations that would otherwise produce coarser equilibrium morphologies.
High-temperature annealing allows the alloy components to intermix and establishes competing phase-formation pathways.
Water quenching halts diffusion sufficiently rapidly to prevent phase growth and coarsening.
Water-quenched specimens will have a higher volume fraction and finer dispersion of metastable phase interfaces than furnace-cooled specimens.
Water quenching will produce a more optimal FCC/BCC balance than furnace cooling.
Water-quenched specimens will exhibit enhanced high-temperature strength relative to furnace-cooled specimens.
Water-quenched specimens will exhibit improved radiation tolerance relative to furnace-cooled specimens.
Water-quenched specimens will exhibit superior environmental resistance relative to furnace-cooled specimens.
Water-quenched specimens will maintain or increase cryogenic toughness relative to furnace-cooled specimens.
Slow cooling after the same annealing treatment produces coarser phase distributions and a potentially less favorable combination of properties.
The proposed quench effect occurs only within an annealing-temperature window that promotes phase mixing while avoiding full equilibrium transformation.
The quench effect may depend on the initial alloy composition and prior processing history.
Outside the applicable processing window, quenching may not change phase dispersion or improve the targeted properties.
